# FEAT-008: Recorder (Phase 1)

> **Status**: [/] In progress
> **Owner**: workflow team
> **Depends on**: FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI), FEAT-002 (Protocol — `LocatorChain`, `CapturedAction` shape), FEAT-003 (BrowserProvider — visible session, ephemeral profile), FEAT-004 (Locator engine — candidate ranking algorithm)
> **Unblocks**: FEAT-009 (Annotate UI & Workflow YAML), FEAT-010 (Workflow Replay)

---

## 1. Feature Goal

Let a non-developer record a browser workflow in a **visible Chrome session** and emit a structured `draft.json` containing the captured actions plus a ranked locator-candidate chain per action. Hand the draft off to FEAT-009 for annotation. Optimize for **trust**: the user sees what's being captured live (recording indicator, action counter), the recorder never reads form values to disk, and the run leaves an inspectable artifact even when it crashes.

The recorder is the **trust mechanism** of Yantra. A user who recorded a workflow understands what it does, because they performed every step in front of a visible browser with a live indicator. There is no AI in this loop — recording is 100% deterministic and tagged `@no-llm`.

**MVP delivery**:

- Visible Chrome session via FEAT-003 `BrowserProvider`, launched against a fresh **ephemeral per-workflow user-data-dir** (no cookie bleed from a real profile unless `--profile` opt-in).
- **CDP-injected overlay** (NOT a Chrome Extension — per plan §7 architectural decision) that draws a recording indicator and forwards in-page events to Node.
- Captures `click`, `fill`, `navigate`, `wait` actions; emits **top-5 ranked locator candidates per action** using FEAT-004's ranking algorithm against the live DOM.
- **Form values redacted at capture time** — the raw `value` of any `fill` is replaced with `<redacted>` _before_ the action is persisted. The original string never leaves page memory and never touches disk.
- Popup / new-tab handling: `window.open` and `target=_blank` produce a CDP `Target.targetCreated` event; the session attaches to the new target and continues capturing. The user is told via the terminal that recording followed the popup.
- Auto-stop on idle (configurable, default 5 minutes) with a terminal prompt.
- Crash safety: if the page crashes mid-recording, the draft is preserved up to the last successful capture and a `RecordingAbortedEvent` is surfaced with a clear next step.

**Non-goals (deferred)**:

- The annotate UI and YAML emission — these are FEAT-009. This feature stops at `draft.json`.
- Reanchor on replay — FEAT-010 (deterministic) and Phase 2 (LLM reanchor).
- Reusing a user's real Chrome profile by default. Opt-in via `--profile <name>` is a Phase 2 enhancement; MVP records against an ephemeral profile only.
- A Chrome Extension. Plan §7 explicitly rejects the extension path for MVP; we revisit only if injected-script reliability becomes a wall (tracked in TODO).
- Capturing keyboard shortcuts other than `Enter` (e.g., `Tab` navigation, hotkeys). Phase 2.

---

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

The recorder has **two persistence surfaces**: an on-disk recording directory and a set of in-memory entities maintained by the Node-side `RecordingSession`. No relational DB in MVP; a Future DB Schema sketch is at the end of this section for Phase 2 migration.

### 2.1 On-Disk Artifacts

All recordings live under `~/.cache/yantra/recording-<uuid>/` (uses `os.tmpdir()` on Windows when `~/.cache` is not present — `BrowserProvider` already normalizes per-OS, FEAT-003). The UUID is generated at `RecordingSession.start()` time.

```
~/.cache/yantra/recording-<uuid>/
  profile/                      # Ephemeral Chrome user-data-dir for THIS recording.
                                # Owned by BrowserProvider; destroyed on stop() unless --keep-profile.
  draft.json                    # The final draft, written atomically on stop().
                                # Pre-annotation; consumed by FEAT-009.
  draft.partial.json            # Written after every CapturedAction (defense-in-depth on crash).
                                # Replaced atomically by draft.json on clean stop().
  events.jsonl                  # Per-action audit trail for debugging: RecordingStarted,
                                # CaptureEmitted, NavigationCaptured, PopupAttached,
                                # RecordingAborted, RecordingStopped. NEVER contains raw values.
  metadata.json                 # start_ts, end_ts, OS, Chrome version, target URL, capture
                                # count, dwell time per page. Used by FEAT-012 audit/show.
```

**Path conventions**:

- `recording-<uuid>` prefix matches the plan's `runs/<run-id>` natural-sort convention; `<uuid>` is a ULID (lexicographic time-ordering) so `ls -1 ~/.cache/yantra/ | sort` produces chronological order.
- Profile dir is **always inside** the recording dir for MVP. Phase 2 will allow `--profile <named>` to point at `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<name>/` instead (FEAT-009 territory).
- Tilde expansion is centralized in FEAT-001's path utility; this feature consumes it, never re-implements it.

**`draft.json` shape** (validated by Zod — see TASK-010):

```jsonc
{
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "recording_id": "01HQ...",
  "workflow_name_hint": "bank-statement",     // From RecordingSession.start(name); the user can rename in annotate.
  "started_at": "2026-05-11T12:34:56.789Z",
  "stopped_at": "2026-05-11T12:42:01.123Z",
  "stop_reason": "user" | "idle_timeout" | "crash" | "page_close",
  "actions": [ /* CapturedAction[] - see §2.2 */ ],
  "metadata": { /* see §2.4 */ }
}
```

**Atomic-write contract**: `draft.json` is written via the FEAT-001 `writeFileAtomic(path, content)` helper (write to `path.tmp` then `rename`) so a crash mid-write never produces a half-flushed file.

### 2.2 In-Memory Entities

All entities live in `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/` and are Zod-validated at every boundary.

#### 2.2.1 `RecordingSession` (`session.ts`)

The Node-side orchestrator. Owns the browser handle, the overlay binding, the redactor, and the draft builder.

| Field              | Type                                                                        | Purpose                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `recordingId`      | `string (ULID)`                                                             | Identifier for the on-disk dir and `events.jsonl` entries.                                  |
| `workflowNameHint` | `string`                                                                    | Passed to `start(name)`; carried into `draft.json` for FEAT-009.                            |
| `recordingDir`     | `string`                                                                    | Absolute path to `~/.cache/yantra/recording-<id>/`.                                         |
| `browser`          | `BrowserProviderHandle` (FEAT-003)                                          | Visible Chrome session pinned to this recording's profile.                                  |
| `cdp`              | `CDPSession`                                                                | Root CDP session used to attach to all targets and inject the overlay.                      |
| `actions`          | `CapturedAction[]`                                                          | Append-only ordered list; flushed to `draft.partial.json` after every push.                 |
| `state`            | `'idle' \| 'recording' \| 'paused' \| 'stopping' \| 'stopped' \| 'aborted'` | State machine; transitions logged to `events.jsonl`.                                        |
| `idleTimerHandle`  | `NodeJS.Timeout \| null`                                                    | Reset on every captured action; fires the idle prompt at the configured threshold.          |
| `popupChain`       | `Map<TargetID, ParentTargetID>`                                             | Tracks `Target.targetCreated` parentage for the user-visible "we just saw a popup" message. |

**Lifecycle methods**:

- `start(workflowName: string, opts?: { idleTimeoutMs?: number; keepProfile?: boolean }): Promise<RecordingHandle>` — creates the recording dir, launches Chrome via FEAT-003 with `headful: true` and a fresh profile, attaches CDP, registers the overlay via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, sets up `Target.targetCreated` listener, transitions to `recording`.
- `stop(reason: StopReason): Promise<{ draftPath: string }>` — flushes any pending action, writes `draft.json` atomically, closes the browser cleanly, destroys the ephemeral profile (unless `keepProfile`), transitions to `stopped`.
- `abort(cause: AbortCause): Promise<{ draftPath: string }>` — same as `stop` but transitions to `aborted` and writes a `stop_reason: "crash"` draft; preserves whatever actions were captured.

#### 2.2.2 `CapturedAction` (`session.ts` / re-exported from `packages/protocol`)

The single shape that flows from in-page → Node-side → `draft.json` → FEAT-009.

```ts
type CapturedAction =
  | {
      kind: 'click';
      element_descriptor: ElementDescriptor;
      candidate_chain: RankedCandidate[];
      ts: string;
      url_before: string;
      url_after: string | null;
    }
  | {
      kind: 'fill';
      element_descriptor: ElementDescriptor;
      candidate_chain: RankedCandidate[];
      ts: string;
      url_before: string;
      url_after: string | null;
      raw_value: '<redacted>';
      value_length: number;
      input_type: InputTypeHint;
    }
  | {
      kind: 'navigate';
      ts: string;
      url_before: string;
      url_after: string;
      navigation_kind: 'user_click' | 'programmatic' | 'address_bar' | 'history' | 'popup';
      triggered_by_action_index: number | null;
    }
  | {
      kind: 'wait';
      ts: string;
      reason: 'dom_content_loaded' | 'network_idle' | 'manual_dwell';
      duration_ms: number;
      url: string;
    };
```

Notes:

- `ts` is the **page-clock timestamp**, captured in-page via `performance.now() + performance.timeOrigin` and converted to ISO-8601 by the Node side. This matters when reasoning about ordering across navigations.
- `url_before` / `url_after` are **always written**, including for `fill` (URLs do change on autocomplete-driven navigation). `url_after` is `null` if no navigation occurred within 500 ms of the action.
- `fill.raw_value` is the literal string `'<redacted>'` — a `z.literal('<redacted>')` in the schema. **No other value is legal.** This is the structural half of the redaction guarantee (see §6 Security and TASK-007).
- `fill.value_length` is preserved (number of code points the user typed) because FEAT-009's annotate UI needs to render `••••••• (8 chars)` so the user can tell apart a password field from a username field they redacted. Length is **not** PII per memory.md §Security.
- `fill.input_type` is one of `'text' | 'email' | 'password' | 'tel' | 'number' | 'url' | 'search' | 'textarea' | 'other'` — purely structural metadata from the DOM, no value content.
- `navigate.triggered_by_action_index` points to the index of the prior `click` action that produced this navigation (TASK-005's heuristic). `null` for `programmatic`, `address_bar`, `history`.
- `wait` actions are recorded only for **manual dwells** > 1500 ms between user actions on the same URL — they signal "the user is reading something" and inform FEAT-010's auto-wait planner. Not every DOM event is a wait.

#### 2.2.3 `ElementDescriptor` (`session.ts`)

A **sanitized structural fingerprint** of the captured target element. Built **in-page** during the event burst, so the descriptor reflects the DOM as the user actually saw it.

```ts
interface ElementDescriptor {
  tag: string; // lowercase, e.g., 'button'
  role: string | null; // ARIA computed role (accname-computation lite)
  accessible_name: string | null; // ARIA accessible-name computation, truncated to 200 chars
  visible_text: string | null; // innerText truncated to 200 chars, normalized whitespace
  attrs_sample: Partial<
    Record<
      | 'id'
      | 'name'
      | 'data-testid'
      | 'data-qa'
      | 'data-cy'
      | 'placeholder'
      | 'aria-label'
      | 'href'
      | 'type',
      string
    >
  >;
  // ONLY these keys are sampled. Other attrs are dropped.
  // Values are sanitized: max 100 chars, control chars stripped.
  bounding_rect: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
  in_iframe: boolean; // true if the element lives in a frame; frame URL stored in candidate_chain context.
  xpath_for_debug: string; // ONLY shown in --debug; not used by replay. Capped at 200 chars.
}
```

**Sanitization rules for `attrs_sample`** (enforced in-page before the descriptor leaves the page):

- `value` and `checked` attributes are **never** sampled. The descriptor exists to identify the _element_, not its state.
- For `<input type="password">`, the `placeholder` is sampled but `aria-label` and accessible name are checked against a small allowlist (`password`, `passcode`, `pin`, ...) — if the accessible name is _not_ one of these and the input is type=password, we replace it with `'<password-field>'` (defense against sites that put the user's password in the aria-label). Logged at `debug`.
- All sampled string values are truncated to 100 chars, control characters (`\x00-\x1f`) stripped, and run through a single defang regex that removes common credential-shape leaks (`sk-...`, `ghp_...`, `AKIA...`, `eyJ...`). The defanged value is replaced with `'<defanged>'` and a debug event is emitted. This is **defense-in-depth** on top of the structural redaction in §2.2.2.

#### 2.2.4 `RankedCandidate` (consumed from FEAT-004)

```ts
interface RankedCandidate {
  candidate: LocatorChain; // Discriminated union from packages/protocol (FEAT-002 §2.1.2)
  score: number; // 0..1; FEAT-004's ranking algorithm output
  rank_reason: string; // Short human label, e.g., "data-testid match", "role+name match", "unique-CSS fallback"
}
```

A `candidate_chain: RankedCandidate[]` is **always exactly 5 entries** if 5 candidates can be generated; fewer if the element is so sparse that FEAT-004 returns < 5. The recorder does not pad with junk locators — an `candidate_chain` of length 1 is a legitimate signal to FEAT-009 ("this element is fragile") and the annotate UI warns the user.

#### 2.2.5 `RecorderOverlayState` (in-page only)

Lives in the page's window scope under `window.__yantraRecorder`. The Node side never reads it back — it exists for the UI overlay.

```ts
interface RecorderOverlayState {
  status: 'recording' | 'paused';
  actionCount: number;
  lastActionAt: number; // performance.now() of last capture
  toastQueue: ToastMessage[];
}
```

Posted as a serialized payload via a CDP binding for each state change (TASK-001/TASK-002).

### 2.3 Repository-Style Interfaces

Per memory.md §Design Patterns ("Repository-like abstractions for persistence boundaries"). These are the seams that Phase 2 will swap for the SQLite-backed equivalent.

#### 2.3.1 `RecordingStore` (`store.ts`)

```ts
interface RecordingStore {
  /** Create the recording dir + profile dir; idempotent on retry. */
  create(
    recordingId: string,
    workflowNameHint: string,
  ): Promise<{ recordingDir: string; profileDir: string }>;

  /** Append a captured action to the partial draft. Writes atomically. */
  appendAction(recordingId: string, action: CapturedAction): Promise<void>;

  /** Finalize: validate full draft against Zod, write draft.json atomically, return its path. */
  saveDraft(recordingId: string, draft: RecordingDraft): Promise<string>;

  /** Read a draft for FEAT-009 consumption. Validates on load. */
  loadDraft(recordingId: string): Promise<RecordingDraft>;

  /** Destroy the recording dir, including the profile, unless keepProfile=true. */
  destroy(recordingId: string, opts: { keepProfile: boolean }): Promise<void>;
}
```

Default implementation: `FileSystemRecordingStore` using `fs/promises`. Phase 2 will introduce `SqliteRecordingStore` (sketched in §2.5) that keeps the filesystem profile but moves drafts and metadata into a table.

#### 2.3.2 `CaptureRedactor` (`redactor.ts`)

```ts
interface CaptureRedactor {
  /** Strip raw values from a fill action BEFORE it crosses any persistence boundary.
   * Idempotent. Returns a NEW object — never mutates the input. */
  redact(action: CapturedActionInput): CapturedAction;
}
```

- `CapturedActionInput` is the in-page-emitted shape that DOES carry a `raw_value: string`. The redactor is the **only place** that field is ever read, and it is read only to compute `value_length` before discarding the value.
- The default implementation `DefaultCaptureRedactor` enforces:
  - Replace `raw_value` with the literal `'<redacted>'`.
  - Compute and preserve `value_length = [...rawValue].length` (code-point count, not byte count).
  - Carry over `input_type` from the input action.
  - Zero the input's `raw_value` buffer with `Buffer.fill(0)` best-effort (per memory.md §Security).
- The redactor runs **before** `RecordingStore.appendAction` — the call site (in `session.ts`) is enforced by TypeScript: `appendAction` accepts `CapturedAction` (post-redaction shape), not `CapturedActionInput`. Attempting to skip the redactor is a type error.

### 2.4 Recording Metadata Schema

Written to `metadata.json` and embedded into `draft.json` under `metadata`. Consumed by FEAT-012 `yantra audit`/`yantra show`.

```ts
interface RecordingMetadata {
  start_ts: string; // ISO-8601
  end_ts: string | null; // null until stop() / abort()
  os: { platform: NodeJS.Platform; release: string; arch: string };
  chrome_version: string; // Full version string from `Browser.getVersion` CDP call (e.g., "124.0.6367.91")
  chrome_major: number; // Parsed from chrome_version; surfaced separately to map cleanly into
  // WorkflowFile.recorded_with.chrome_major (FEAT-002 §2.1.9) and to power
  // the FEAT-010 Chrome-drift advisory at replay (plan §6).
  yantra_version: string; // From package.json — also flows into WorkflowFile.recorded_with.yantra_version
  initial_url: string; // The first navigation captured (often about:blank → user-typed)
  capture_count: number;
  dwell_per_page: Array<{ url: string; ms: number }>;
  stop_reason: 'user' | 'idle_timeout' | 'crash' | 'page_close';
  // Cross-origin iframes encountered but not instrumented during this recording. FEAT-008 TASK-006a
  // populates; FEAT-009 lifts into WorkflowFile._unrecorded_frames; FEAT-010 reads at replay time.
  unrecorded_frame_origins: string[];
}
```

### 2.5 Future DB Schema (Phase 2 — not implemented in this feature)

```sql
-- Sketch only; Phase 2 will move drafts to SQLite, keep the on-disk profile dir.
CREATE TABLE recordings (
  recording_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- ULID
  workflow_name_hint TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  stopped_at TEXT,
  stop_reason TEXT NOT NULL,
  chrome_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  initial_url TEXT NOT NULL,
  metadata_json TEXT NOT NULL           -- The full RecordingMetadata blob
);

CREATE TABLE captured_actions (
  recording_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recordings(recording_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  action_index INTEGER NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('click','fill','navigate','wait')),
  ts TEXT NOT NULL,
  url_before TEXT,
  url_after TEXT,
  element_descriptor_json TEXT,         -- Null for navigate/wait
  candidate_chain_json TEXT,            -- Null for navigate/wait
  extra_json TEXT,                      -- value_length, input_type, navigation_kind, etc.
  PRIMARY KEY (recording_id, action_index)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_actions_recording ON captured_actions(recording_id, action_index);
```

The MVP filesystem layout is forward-compatible: each `draft.json.actions[i]` maps 1:1 to a `captured_actions` row.

### 2.6 Redaction Rules (Authoritative)

This is the structural guarantee the security tests pin to. **Every clause is enforced by tests.**

| Rule                                                                                                            | Mechanism                                                                                                   | Test                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CapturedAction` of kind `fill` has `raw_value: '<redacted>'` exactly                                           | Zod `z.literal('<redacted>')`; type system rejects any other value                                          | TASK-007 unit test                                              |
| The original typed value is read at most once, only by `CaptureRedactor.redact`, only to compute `value_length` | Linter rule + code review checklist: `raw_value` is referenced only inside `redactor.ts`                    | TASK-007 property test                                          |
| No `RawCapturedActionInput` leaves the recorder module boundary                                                 | Exported types from `index.ts` exclude `RawCapturedActionInput`                                             | TS compiler                                                     |
| No PII from `ElementDescriptor.attrs_sample` survives sanitization                                              | In-page sanitizer truncates + defangs; descriptor passes through Zod on Node side                           | TASK-003 property test                                          |
| `draft.json` after a recording with N typed strings contains zero substrings matching any of those strings      | Property test: generate random strings, type them, then `for each str ∈ typed: assert !draft.includes(str)` | TASK-007 property test (memory.md §Testing mandates this style) |
| `events.jsonl` never contains a raw value or descriptor attribute exceeding 100 chars                           | Logger redactor at the pino sink layer                                                                      | Snapshot test                                                   |

## 3. Files

All paths are relative to the monorepo root. Test files mirror the source tree under `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/` (per memory.md §Project Structure — co-located is fine; we choose mirrored here because the overlay bundle has its own test surface).

### 3.1 In-Page (browser-runtime) sources

These are bundled by esbuild into a single IIFE shipped via CDP. They run in the page, never in Node.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/index.ts`
  Entry point for the injected script. Registers `window.__yantraRecorder`. Draws the recording UI (top-right indicator, action counter, "stop available via terminal" hint). Sets up the CDP binding `__yantraRecorderEmit(payload)` for posting events to Node. No dependencies on Node-side modules — checked by the bundle build step.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/event-listeners.ts`
  Capturing-phase document-level listeners: `click`, `input` (debounced 250 ms per element), `change`, `submit`, `keydown` (only `Enter`). On each event: build the `ElementDescriptor` in-page, attach the raw input value, post to Node via `__yantraRecorderEmit`. Listens to `DOMContentLoaded`, `load`, `popstate` for navigation observation; canonical navigation events come from CDP Node-side (TASK-005), these are belt-and-braces.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/descriptor-builder.ts`
  In-page `buildElementDescriptor(el: Element): ElementDescriptor` — implements ARIA accname computation (lite), attribute sampling, sanitization. Imported by `event-listeners.ts`. Has its own jsdom-based unit test surface.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/bundle.ts`
  esbuild config (called as a programmatic API, not a CLI) that produces `packages/core/dist/recorder-overlay.iife.js` — a single IIFE bundle with no externals, ready to feed to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. Treeshakes; banner contains a generation timestamp. The bundle is rebuilt by `pnpm --filter @yantra/core build`.

### 3.2 Node-side sources

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/session.ts`
  Exports the `RecordingSession` class. Owns lifecycle. Composes `BrowserProvider` (FEAT-003), `RecordingStore`, `CaptureRedactor`, `DraftBuilder`, `PopupHandler`. Public methods: `start`, `stop`, `abort`, plus an `EventEmitter`-style interface for `events.jsonl` consumers (and FEAT-012's terminal UI).

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/draft-builder.ts`
  Pure function library: `assembleDraft(actions, metadata, hint, recordingId, startedAt, stoppedAt, stopReason): RecordingDraft`. Validates against the protocol Zod schema before returning. No I/O — that's the store's job.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/redactor.ts`
  Exports `CaptureRedactor` interface and `DefaultCaptureRedactor` class. Zero dependencies beyond the protocol package's types.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/popup-handler.ts`
  Subscribes to root CDP `Target.targetCreated` / `Target.targetDestroyed`. For each new target whose `openerId` is the current session's main target, attaches a fresh CDP session, injects the same overlay, and tracks parentage in `RecordingSession.popupChain`. Emits a user-visible terminal toast "we just saw a popup — recording continues there" via the events stream.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/store.ts`
  `FileSystemRecordingStore` implementation of the `RecordingStore` interface. Uses `fs/promises` and the FEAT-001 atomic-write helper.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/candidate-resolver.ts`
  Node-side glue: given an in-page-built `ElementDescriptor` plus the live DOM (accessed via CDP `DOM.*` / `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`), calls FEAT-004's ranking algorithm and returns `RankedCandidate[]` of length up to 5. **All candidate generation happens here**, not in-page — that keeps FEAT-004 the single source of truth for locator scoring.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/idle-watcher.ts`
  Sets / resets a timer on every captured action. On fire: emits a terminal prompt via the events stream ("still recording — stop now?"); the session keeps running until the user responds.

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/index.ts`
  Public barrel. Exports `RecordingSession`, `RecordingDraft` type, `RecordingMetadata` type, the stop-reason enum. **Does not** export `RawCapturedActionInput` or any in-page-only types.

### 3.3 Protocol package additions

- `packages/protocol/src/schemas/recording-draft.ts`
  Zod schema for `RecordingDraft`, `CapturedAction`, `ElementDescriptor`, `RankedCandidate`, `RecordingMetadata`. Re-exported from `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`. The `fill` variant's `raw_value` is `z.literal('<redacted>')` — this is the type-level half of the redaction guarantee.

### 3.4 Tests (mirrored, heavy integration)

- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/session.spec.ts` — unit: state machine, lifecycle, error paths.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/redactor.spec.ts` — unit + property test (TASK-007).
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/draft-builder.spec.ts` — unit: assemble/validate.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/store.spec.ts` — unit: atomic write, partial flush, destroy.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/popup-handler.spec.ts` — integration: drives a fixture page with `window.open`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/__tests__/idle-watcher.spec.ts` — unit: fake timers.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/__tests__/descriptor-builder.spec.ts` — unit with jsdom.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/overlay/__tests__/event-listeners.spec.ts` — unit with jsdom + simulated DOM events.
- `e2e/recorder/login-form.spec.ts` — heavy integration: drives recorder against a fixture login + table page; asserts draft contents (TASK-011).
- `e2e/recorder/popup-flow.spec.ts` — heavy integration: fixture page with `target=_blank`.
- `e2e/recorder/crash-preserves-draft.spec.ts` — heavy integration: crashes the page mid-recording (CDP `Page.crash`), asserts `draft.json` exists with `stop_reason: "crash"`.

Fixture pages live under `e2e/recorder/fixtures/` — pure static HTML served by `http-server` on a random port, no JS frameworks.

## 4. Dependencies

### Internal

- **FEAT-001** — pnpm workspace, build pipeline, atomic-write helper, path-utility.
- **FEAT-002** — `LocatorChain` discriminated union (consumed by `RankedCandidate.candidate`); `RecordingDraft` schema authoring lives in `packages/protocol` per FEAT-002's "schemas are the data model" doctrine.
- **FEAT-003** — `BrowserProvider.launch({ headful: true, profileDir, transport: 'pipe' })` is the only way this feature opens Chrome. The ephemeral-profile semantics (create fresh, destroy on close) are owned by FEAT-003; this feature consumes the contract.
- **FEAT-004** — the locator-engine candidate-ranking algorithm. `candidate-resolver.ts` is a thin adapter calling FEAT-004's public function. **Critical dependency**: if FEAT-004 ships with a different ranking-function signature than expected, this feature must rev with it. Flagged as a TODO follow-up to lock the signature early.

### External (npm)

- `esbuild` — already in the FEAT-001 toolchain; used here for the in-page overlay bundle.
- `puppeteer-core` — already FEAT-003's dep; this feature uses CDP only, no high-level puppeteer APIs.
- `ulid` — for `recording_id` generation (lexicographic time-ordering for natural sort).
- `fs/promises` (Node builtin) — store I/O.

No new top-level npm dependencies introduced by this feature beyond `ulid`. `ulid` is unmaintained-but-stable; alternative is `nanoid` with a separate timestamp prefix — flagged as a TODO follow-up to revisit before MVP ship.

---

## 5. Implementation Tasks

The tasks below are vertical slices. Each ships a runnable, testable subset. A working `yantra record bank-statement` is the cumulative output of TASK-001 through TASK-010; TASK-011 through TASK-014 harden it.

### TASK-001 — Recorder overlay bundle (esbuild + IIFE + CDP injection)

- Author `overlay/bundle.ts` calling esbuild's programmatic API; output: `dist/recorder-overlay.iife.js` (no externals, ES2022, minified in CI, dev-readable locally).
- Wire bundle generation into the package's `build` script.
- Author `overlay/index.ts`: registers `window.__yantraRecorder = { state, emit, ... }`; draws a `position: fixed; top: 8px; right: 8px;` recording indicator (red dot + action counter); draws a transient toast slot for popup notifications. **No "stop" click target** — the overlay tells the user "stop with Ctrl+C in the terminal" to avoid the recursive problem of the stop button being captured as a click action.
- In `session.start()`, register the bundle via CDP `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` **before** the first navigation, so the overlay loads on every navigation including the initial one.
- Unit test (jsdom): renders the overlay, verifies the indicator appears and the action counter updates when `window.__yantraRecorder.emit(...)` is called.

**Acceptance**: a manually-launched session shows the red indicator immediately on `about:blank`; navigating to any URL keeps the indicator across page loads.

### TASK-002 — In-page event listeners + CDP binding

- Author `overlay/event-listeners.ts`. Capturing-phase, document-level: `click`, `input` (250 ms debounce per element, keyed by a `WeakMap` of element → last-flush-time), `change`, `submit`, `keydown` (only `key === 'Enter'`).
- For each event: build the `ElementDescriptor` (TASK-003), grab `event.target`'s current `value` if the target is an `<input>` or `<textarea>`, emit `{ kind, descriptor, raw_value, ts: performance.now() + performance.timeOrigin, url: location.href }` via `window.__yantraRecorderEmit(JSON.stringify(payload))`.
- Node side: pre-`start`, call `Runtime.addBinding({ name: '__yantraRecorderEmit' })`, then listen on `Runtime.bindingCalled`; parse + Zod-validate the payload as a `RawCapturedActionInput`; pass through `CaptureRedactor`; push to `actions`; flush partial draft.
- **Critical sequencing**: the binding is registered on every new CDP session (main + popups). Popup-handler (TASK-006) re-registers.

**Acceptance**: typing in a fixture login form produces, in order: input events on the username field, an `Enter` keydown event, a click on Submit — surfaced in `events.jsonl` as four `CapturedAction`s.

### TASK-003 — ElementDescriptor builder (in-page)

- Author `overlay/descriptor-builder.ts`. Function: `buildElementDescriptor(el: Element): ElementDescriptor`.
- Compute ARIA role using a lite re-implementation of accname-computation (the full WAI spec is too heavy for an injected script; we cover the common 90% — explicit `role` attr, then implicit role from `tag` + relevant attrs).
- Compute accessible name in this priority: `aria-labelledby` → `aria-label` → `<label for>` → `<label>` parent → text content → `placeholder` → `title`. Truncate to 200 chars.
- Sample attrs from the whitelist set only. Apply sanitization per §2.2.3 (truncate, defang, password-field aria-label allowlist).
- Compute bounding rect via `el.getBoundingClientRect()`.
- Detect iframe ownership via `el.ownerDocument !== document.defaultView.document`.
- Capture `xpath_for_debug` via a minimal absolute-XPath generator, capped at 200 chars.
- Unit tests (jsdom): table-driven cases for buttons with `aria-label`, inputs with associated `<label for>`, password fields, elements inside Shadow DOM (open-mode supported; closed-mode falls back to `'<closed-shadow>'` placeholder).

**Acceptance**: descriptor for a `<button data-testid="submit">Sign in</button>` has `tag='button'`, `role='button'`, `accessible_name='Sign in'`, `attrs_sample={ 'data-testid': 'submit' }`.

### TASK-004 — Candidate-chain generator (Node-side, on each captured action)

- Author `candidate-resolver.ts`. Function: `async resolveCandidates(descriptor: ElementDescriptor, cdp: CDPSession): Promise<RankedCandidate[]>`.
- Locate the live element on the page using the descriptor — primary path: `Runtime.evaluate` with an expression that recomputes a small candidate set in-page and returns the matching `nodeId`. Fallback: `DOM.querySelectorAll` against a CSS derived from `descriptor.tag` + the most distinctive attr.
- With the live element node, call FEAT-004's `rankCandidates(node, cdp)` and take the top 5.
- If FEAT-004 returns fewer than 5 candidates, return what it gives — do not pad. The chain length is informational signal for the annotate UI.
- If FEAT-004 fails (rare; bug class), log at `warn`, emit a `RecordingDegradedEvent`, and record the action with a single-element `candidate_chain` containing the descriptor's `xpath_for_debug` as a `LocatorChain.kind = 'xpath'` of last resort — this guarantees an action is always saveable.

**Acceptance**: an integration test against a fixture page asserts: for a button with `[data-testid=login]`, the top-ranked candidate is `{ kind: 'testid', value: 'login', ... }` with score > 0.9.

### TASK-005 — Navigation capture (CDP `Page.frameNavigated`)

- Subscribe to `Page.frameNavigated` for the main frame on every attached target.
- For each navigation: emit a `CapturedAction { kind: 'navigate', ... }`.
- Classify `navigation_kind`:
  - If a `click` action was recorded within 1000 ms before the navigation **and** the clicked element was an `<a>` or `<button type=submit>` or had `role=link`, mark `navigation_kind: 'user_click'` and set `triggered_by_action_index` to that click.
  - If the navigation comes from a CDP `Page.frameRequestedNavigation` with `reason: 'scriptInitiated'`, mark `programmatic`.
  - History API (`pushState`/`replaceState`/`popstate`): mark `history`.
  - Otherwise: `address_bar`.
- Backfill `url_after` on the prior action(s) that occurred on `url_before`.

**Acceptance**: clicking a `<a href="/dashboard">` produces one `click` action followed by one `navigate` action with `navigation_kind: 'user_click'` and `triggered_by_action_index` pointing at the click.

### TASK-006 — Popup / new-tab handling (CDP `Target.targetCreated`)

- Subscribe to root `Target.targetCreated`.
- Filter on `targetInfo.type === 'page'` and `openerId === <current session's main target ID>` (or recursively, opener within `popupChain`).
- For each matching new target: call `Target.attachToTarget({ targetId, flatten: true })`, get the resulting `CDPSession`, re-register the overlay binding, re-inject the overlay via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, store parentage in `popupChain`.
- Emit a `PopupOpenedEvent` on the session's event stream — FEAT-012's terminal UI renders this as "→ recording followed a popup (now on `https://...`)".
- On `Target.targetDestroyed` for a popup, emit `PopupClosedEvent` and resume capture on the parent if it is the currently-foreground target.

**Acceptance**: a fixture page with a `<a target="_blank" href="/popup">` link produces a `PopupOpenedEvent`, and subsequent clicks inside the popup are captured in the same `draft.json` (in order).

### TASK-006a — Cross-origin iframe detection + `_unrecorded_frames` annotation

> **Plan §7 mandates this**: CDP-injected scripts attach per-frame and do not reliably capture actions inside cross-origin iframes (OAuth/SSO redirects, Plaid/Okta/Auth0 widgets, embedded 3DS). Silently missing captures is the most common reason hand-built browser-automation tools break on the first real banking workflow. MVP acknowledges the limitation with a clear diagnostic rather than masking it.

- Subscribe to `Page.frameAttached` and `Page.frameNavigated` on every attached target. For each frame, attempt to attach via `Target.attachToTarget` with the frame's `frameId`.
- **Same-origin frames**: attach succeeds → inject overlay script via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` → captures flow normally (the existing TASK-001/002 path).
- **Cross-origin frames**: `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` succeeds technically but the script runs in the frame's origin context and cannot reliably communicate back to the recorder due to cross-origin restrictions. Detect this by comparing the frame's `url`'s origin to the main frame's origin (using `new URL(frameUrl).origin !== new URL(mainFrameUrl).origin`).
- On detection, **do not retry instrumentation**. Instead:
  1. Emit a single `UnrecordedFrameEvent { origin, frameId, detected_at }` on the session's event stream (FEAT-012 renders this as a _warning_ tick: `⚠ recorder cannot capture inside cross-origin frame: <origin>`).
  2. Append the origin (deduplicated) to `RecordingMetadata.unrecorded_frame_origins: string[]` — flushed into `draft.json`.
  3. The annotate flow (FEAT-009) reads this and writes the workflow YAML's `_unrecorded_frames` array, where FEAT-010's replay reads it to produce `LOCATOR_MISS_IN_UNRECORDED_FRAME` diagnostics on locator misses against those origins.
- **What we do NOT do**: try to bridge the cross-origin gap via `postMessage`-based heuristics, attach via debugger protocol with `--disable-web-security` flags, or rewrite the iframe's `src` attribute. Each of these is invasive, breaks legitimate site behavior, or is detectable as automation. Honest limitation > clever fragile workaround (plan §15 honesty-over-cleverness).

**Acceptance**: a fixture page that embeds `<iframe src="http://other-origin.example.com/login">` produces exactly one `UnrecordedFrameEvent` with `origin: "http://other-origin.example.com"`; `draft.json.metadata.unrecorded_frame_origins` contains exactly this origin; clicks inside the iframe do not appear in `draft.json.actions` (and the user is warned, not silently misled).

**Test additions**:

- Fixture page with both a same-origin iframe (captured) and a cross-origin iframe (skipped + flagged) — assert exactly the expected partition.
- Fixture with three different cross-origin iframes — assert the metadata list contains all three origins, deduplicated.
- Phase 2 marker: when the Chrome-extension recorder lands (per plan §7 TODO), this task's behavior is replaced. The test fixture for cross-origin captures should survive the migration as a regression guard.

### TASK-007 — Value redaction at capture time (the structural guarantee)

- Author `redactor.ts` per §2.3.2.
- Wire the redactor at the **only** place `RawCapturedActionInput` becomes `CapturedAction`: at the top of `RecordingSession.onActionEmitted(...)`. Mark the call site with a `// SECURITY: only redaction site` comment; CI grep enforces no other call site references `raw_value`.
- Type system: do not export `RawCapturedActionInput` from `recorder/index.ts`. Internal-only type.
- Unit test: feed a synthetic fill action with `raw_value: 'sk-test-xxxxxxxx'`; assert the output has `raw_value: '<redacted>'` and `value_length: 16`.
- **Property test** (fast-check, per memory.md): generate 1000 random strings of varying alphabets and lengths; "type" each into a recording (via a synthetic in-page emission); assert that walking the resulting `draft.json` produces zero substring matches for any of the generated strings. This is the test that pins the guarantee.

**Acceptance**: property test passes 1000+ iterations; CI grep finds no `.raw_value` access outside `redactor.ts` and `redactor.spec.ts`.

### TASK-008 — `RecordingSession.start(workflowName)`

- Generate `recording_id` (ULID); compute `recordingDir = ~/.cache/yantra/recording-<id>/`.
- Call `RecordingStore.create(recordingId, workflowName)`.
- Call `BrowserProvider.launch({ headful: true, profileDir: <recordingDir>/profile, transport: 'pipe' })` (FEAT-003).
- Get `CDPSession`; register `__yantraRecorderEmit` binding (TASK-002); inject overlay bundle via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` (TASK-001); subscribe to navigation (TASK-005) and target lifecycle (TASK-006).
- Read Chrome version via `Browser.getVersion`; build `RecordingMetadata`; persist to `metadata.json`.
- Transition state to `recording`; start idle watcher (TASK-012); return a `RecordingHandle` whose stream emits all events.

**Acceptance**: `yantra record <name>` (using TASK-008 directly from CLI scaffolding in FEAT-012 — this task targets the programmatic API consumed by the CLI) opens visible Chrome, shows the overlay, and writes `metadata.json` immediately.

### TASK-009 — `RecordingSession.stop(reason)`

- Stop accepting new captures (state → `stopping`).
- Flush any in-flight debounced input event.
- Call `DraftBuilder.assembleDraft(...)`; Zod-validate; call `RecordingStore.saveDraft(...)` for atomic write.
- Close the browser cleanly via `BrowserProvider.close()`.
- Call `RecordingStore.destroy(recordingId, { keepProfile })` — destroys the profile dir unless `--keep-profile`.
- State → `stopped`; resolve the `RecordingHandle.done` promise with `{ draftPath }`.
- **SIGINT handler**: registering `process.once('SIGINT', () => session.stop('user'))` in the CLI is FEAT-012's job; this task exposes the `stop(reason: StopReason)` method only.

**Acceptance**: stopping a recording produces `draft.json` validated against the Zod schema; the profile dir is gone; the partial draft is gone; the browser is closed.

### TASK-010 — `RecordingDraft` Zod schema (lives in `packages/protocol`)

- Add `packages/protocol/src/schemas/recording-draft.ts`.
- Define `RecordingDraft`, `CapturedAction` (discriminated union by `kind`), `ElementDescriptor`, `RankedCandidate`, `RecordingMetadata` per §2.
- The `fill` variant has `raw_value: z.literal('<redacted>')` — the _type system_ refuses any other string.
- Re-export from `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`. Updates `verify-exports.ts` (from FEAT-002) to include the new exports.
- Inline `.describe()` on every field per FEAT-002's doctrine — these feed the auto-generated protocol spec doc.
- Snapshot test on the emitted JSON Schema (drift detector).

**Acceptance**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/protocol verify` stays green; `RecordingDraft` appears in `docs/protocol-spec.md` with descriptions.

### TASK-011 — Recorder integration test against a fixture page

- Build a fixture `e2e/recorder/fixtures/login-and-table.html`: a `<form>` with `username` + `password` + `Sign in`; on submit, swaps to a page with a small `<table>` of three rows. Pure static HTML.
- Serve via `http-server` on a random port (Vitest fixture).
- Test: programmatically (via puppeteer-core's own `page.type` and `page.click`) drive the visible session that the recorder is also watching. Verify `draft.json.actions` contains: `navigate`, two `fill`s (with `<redacted>`, correct `value_length`, correct `input_type`), `click`, `navigate (user_click)`, all with `candidate_chain.length >= 1` and the top candidate having score > 0.7.
- Tagged `@no-llm`. Slow (~10–20 s). Lives in the e2e suite; not in the per-package fast unit tier.

**Acceptance**: green in all three OS CI dimensions × `LLM_PROVIDER ∈ {anthropic, none}`.

### TASK-012 — Auto-stop on idle

- Author `idle-watcher.ts`. Default threshold: 5 min (configurable via `RecordingSession` constructor opts).
- On every `appendAction` call, reset the timer.
- On fire: emit `IdleTimeoutPromptEvent` on the session's event stream. **Do not auto-stop** — the user might be reading something. The CLI (FEAT-012) renders the prompt: "still recording — stop now? [y/N]". If `y`, calls `session.stop('idle_timeout')`; if `N`, calls `session.resetIdleTimer()`.
- Configurable via `opts.idleTimeoutMs` (testing uses 100 ms).
- Unit test with `vi.useFakeTimers()`.

**Acceptance**: after 5 min of inactivity, the event stream emits exactly one `IdleTimeoutPromptEvent`; no actions are dropped.

### TASK-013 — Error handling: page crash during recording

- Subscribe to CDP `Inspector.targetCrashed` and `Target.targetDestroyed` for unexpected destruction.
- On crash: build a `RecordingAbortedEvent { cause: 'page_crash', last_action_index, recording_dir }`; emit on the event stream; call `RecordingSession.abort('crash')`.
- `abort('crash')` writes `draft.json` with `stop_reason: 'crash'`, validating that the partial actions list is non-empty (single-step plans are still valid; an empty action list is also valid and produces an empty-but-loadable draft so the user knows the recording session existed).
- The profile dir is preserved (overridden `keepProfile = true` on crash) for post-mortem.
- Browser handle is closed via `BrowserProvider.close({ force: true })` — non-clean shutdown is acceptable on crash.
- FEAT-012's terminal renderer surfaces the abort as: "Recording aborted — page crashed. Partial draft saved to `<path>`. Profile preserved at `<profile-path>` for inspection."

**Acceptance**: a test that calls CDP `Page.crash` mid-recording produces a `draft.json` with `stop_reason: 'crash'` and the captured actions up to that point.

### TASK-014 — Recording metadata

- Build `RecordingMetadata` at `start` time; update incrementally; finalize at `stop`/`abort`.
- `dwell_per_page` is computed from `url_before` transitions: every time `url` changes between actions, the dwell on the prior URL is `(ts_last_action_on_prior - ts_first_action_on_prior)`. Total session dwell = `end_ts - start_ts`.
- `chrome_version` via `Browser.getVersion` CDP call (one-shot at `start`). **`chrome_major`** is parsed from `chrome_version` with a simple `parseInt(version.split('.')[0], 10)` and stored alongside — this is the value that maps into `WorkflowFile.recorded_with.chrome_major` (FEAT-002 §2.1.9) so FEAT-010 can run its drift comparison without re-parsing.
- `yantra_version` read from `packages/core/package.json` at module load.
- `unrecorded_frame_origins`: a `Set<string>` maintained across the session by TASK-006a; flushed as a sorted, deduplicated array at finalize.
- Embed `metadata` into `draft.json` and also write the standalone `metadata.json` (FEAT-012's `yantra show <recording-id>` reads the standalone file for fast listing).

**Acceptance**: a recorded session shows realistic dwell times in `metadata.json` for a 30-second hand-driven scenario; `chrome_major` is a positive integer matching the major component of `chrome_version`; `unrecorded_frame_origins` is an empty array for a recording with no cross-origin frames and a sorted-deduplicated array otherwise.

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

### Auth

- The recorder uses an **ephemeral profile** by default — the `BrowserProvider` (FEAT-003) creates a fresh `<recordingDir>/profile/` per recording and the profile is destroyed at `stop`. No cookies, no localStorage, no extensions — the session is "clean room."
- **Opt-in `--profile <named>` flag** (CLI surface owned by FEAT-012): points at `~/.local/share/yantra/profiles/<name>/`, reusing a user's per-workflow profile if they've already logged in interactively. The recorder treats this profile dir as **read/write** but does not delete it on stop. Documented as an advanced flag.
- The recorder does not capture or proxy authentication — it observes user behavior, including manual logins. If the user types their password during recording, the redactor strips it (it never reaches disk); the `_locators` ranking for the password field still works because it's structural.

### Error Handling

- Every internal failure path emits a typed `RecordingError` (extends `Error`, carries `recordingId`, `stage`, `cause`) and is surfaced to the terminal with a clear next step. Memory.md §Error Handling: "no silent failures."
- **Page crash** → TASK-013 (partial draft preserved).
- **CDP disconnect** (e.g., user kills Chrome from the system) → same path as crash, `cause: 'browser_disconnected'`.
- **Disk full / EACCES on draft write** → emit `RecordingDegradedEvent` with the OS error; keep recording in memory; second attempt on next action; if persistent, abort with `cause: 'disk_unwritable'` and dump actions to the terminal as JSON so the user can copy them.
- **Schema validation failure** when assembling the draft (should be impossible if the in-memory state is well-typed, but defense-in-depth) → log the failing actions, abort with `cause: 'schema_drift'`, point the user at the partial draft for manual inspection.

### Logging

- Pino, structured JSON, per memory.md §Logging. Three sinks:
  1. `events.jsonl` in the recording dir — the canonical observability artifact.
  2. The session's in-process `EventEmitter` — consumed by FEAT-012's terminal UI.
  3. Pino's stdout (only when `--debug` global flag is set).
- Log levels per memory.md:
  - `info` on `RecordingStarted`, `RecordingStopped`, `PopupOpened/Closed`.
  - `debug` per `CapturedAction` (logs the kind, ts, descriptor's `tag` and `role` only — **never** the `raw_value` or `attrs_sample`).
  - `warn` on `RecordingDegradedEvent` (retryable issues).
  - `error` on `RecordingAbortedEvent` (paired with state → `aborted`).
- **Never log raw values, full descriptors, or DOM payloads.** Pino's redactor is configured with paths `['*.raw_value', '*.attrs_sample.*', '*.visible_text', '*.accessible_name']` as defense-in-depth.

### Security

- **The redaction guarantee is structural** (Zod literal type + type-system gating) — not a runtime check that could regress. TASK-007's property test pins it.
- **The ephemeral profile is created fresh + destroyed on stop** unless the user passes `--keep-profile` for debugging. If `--keep-profile`, the terminal explicitly warns: "profile preserved at `<path>` — it may contain cookies; delete manually if sensitive."
- **No literal-credential logging**: pino's redactor + the descriptor's defang regex (§2.2.3) catch common credential shapes (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `AKIA`, `eyJ`) as defense-in-depth. The primary guarantee is structural; the regex is the safety net.
- **CDP transport is pipe**, not WebSocket — per FEAT-003 and memory.md §Security. No exposed localhost ports during recording.
- The recorder **never sends data off-device**. No telemetry. Per memory.md §General: "local-first by default."
- The `xpath_for_debug` field on `ElementDescriptor` is the only path that surfaces full element-context text and is shown only with `--debug`. Production replays do not consume it.

### Testing

- **All recorder tests are `@no-llm`** — the recorder has zero LLM dependencies. Must pass in both `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` and `LLM_PROVIDER=none` CI dimensions (memory.md §Testing).
- **Property-based tests** on the redactor (TASK-007) — mandatory per memory.md §Testing's "property tests for the sanitizer surface" — the redactor is a sanitizer-adjacent surface and gets the same treatment.
- **CDP-integration tests against static HTML fixtures** under `e2e/recorder/fixtures/` — login form, popup flow, crash injection. Slow but deterministic; run nightly + on PRs that touch `packages/core/src/workflow/recorder/**`.
- **Cross-OS coverage from day one** — recorder paths differ on Windows (path separators, `~/.cache` doesn't exist by default → `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Cache\yantra\`). The FEAT-001 path utility normalizes; tests run on all three OS images.
- **No mocking of FEAT-004's ranking algorithm** — recorder integration tests use the real algorithm against real DOMs. If FEAT-004 changes ranking, FEAT-008 tests will surface it (intentional; recorder/locator coupling is load-bearing).

### Status

This section is owned by the Implement skill. The `[ ] Not started` marker at the top of this file is updated to `[/] In progress` when implementation begins and `[x] Complete` when verified per the dogfooding criterion below.

### Dogfooding Acceptance Test (manual, before marking complete)

The author of the implementation must verify, before flipping the status:

1. `pnpm --filter @yantra/core build` succeeds clean on a fresh checkout on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu; the overlay IIFE bundle is produced.
2. `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test` passes 100% in both `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic` and `LLM_PROVIDER=none` CI dimensions, including the property-based redaction test.
3. From a fresh shell, run a recording against a real public site (the developer chooses one — e.g., `example.com` + a small interaction sequence). Visible Chrome opens, the overlay is visible, the recording follows two manual navigations.
4. Stop the recording with Ctrl+C. Confirm `~/.cache/yantra/recording-<id>/draft.json` exists, parses, and contains at least one `click`, one `fill`, and two `navigate` actions with non-empty `candidate_chain` arrays.
5. `grep -r '<the-password-you-typed>' ~/.cache/yantra/recording-<id>/` returns **zero** matches. (Memory.md §Security pinning.)
6. Repeat the recording with `--keep-profile`. Confirm the warning surfaces and the profile dir survives.
7. Trigger a popup recording flow (open any site with `target="_blank"` links); confirm the terminal renders "→ recording followed a popup" and the popup's actions appear in `draft.json` in order.

## Deviations Flagged

- **No "stop" click target inside the overlay UI.** Plan §2 sketches one; this spec drops it because a click on the stop button would itself be captured as a `CapturedAction`, polluting the draft. Stop is terminal-only (Ctrl+C → SIGINT handler in FEAT-012). The overlay shows a hint: "stop with Ctrl+C in the terminal."
- **`value_length` is preserved post-redaction** on `fill` actions. Not in the plan brief; introduced here because FEAT-009's annotate UI needs to render `••••••• (8 chars)` so the user can distinguish username/password fields they want to promote to params vs secrets. Length is not PII per memory.md §Security but flagged for awareness.
- **Candidate generation runs Node-side, not in-page.** The plan brief is ambiguous; the brainstorm §8.2 implies in-page. Moving it Node-side keeps FEAT-004 (the locator engine) as the single source of truth for ranking — in-page candidate generation would force a duplicate ranking implementation inside the overlay bundle and a CSP-incompatible code path. Trade-off: one extra round-trip per action; acceptable for a human-driven recorder.
- **No keyboard shortcut capture other than `Enter`.** Brainstorm §8.1 lists `Tab` as a captured event; this spec drops `Tab` because keyboard focus changes are not workflow-meaningful unless they're paired with a value entry (which `input`/`change` already captures). Phase 2 may revisit for accessibility flows.
- **`recording-<uuid>` lives under `~/.cache/yantra/`, not `~/.local/share/yantra/`.** Plan §4 puts runs under `~/.local/share`; this spec scopes the recorder's intermediate artifacts to `~/.cache` because they're disposable until promoted to a workflow (FEAT-009). The annotate flow's emitted YAML goes to `~/.local/share/yantra/workflows/`. Following the XDG conventions for "cache" vs "data."
- **`navigation_kind: 'user_click'` heuristic uses a 1000 ms window.** Not in the plan brief; introduced as the simplest defensible heuristic for clicker→navigator correlation. May need tuning during dogfooding.
- **`RawCapturedActionInput` is an internal type that is deliberately not exported.** Forces every consumer outside this module to deal with the post-redaction `CapturedAction`. The redactor is the only legal crossing point; CI grep enforces no leak.
